title: Fit a table lamp harp and shade
instruction: Fit the harp into the lamp, lower both retaining sleeves, and seat the shade on the harp.
context: Paxton Hardware’s 8-inch removable lamp harp, SKU 1231A, uses the same saddle and sleeve mechanism documented in RH’s Lattice Table Lamp instructions. The legs squeeze into the saddle notches. The sleeves keep the legs captured while the harp carries the shade. The task ends with the shade resting on the harp, ready for the finial.
setup: On a level 1100 × 1300 mm tabletop, use an unpowered lamp with an empty B&P 48303 socket over the saddle supplied with Paxton 1231A. The physical lamp uses a B&P 10062A 5½-inch base and a B&P 22240 1/8 IPS stem with the saddle underside 99 mm above the table. Stand the 203.2 mm steel harp in a 69 × 135 × 9 mm metal rest with two open foot channels and both sleeves down. Use a fabric spider shade with a 142 mm top, 216 mm bottom, 139 mm height and 11.11 mm washer bore. A loose 24 mm finial stays on the table.
scoring: 0.5 when both feet are captured and both sleeves retain them with the hands clear. Check each foot visually before lowering the sleeves, then check that both rims cover their wings and neither foot withdraws during a gentle individual upward check. 1.0 when the shade washer is seated and the entire assembly is upright, tabletop-supported and stable for one second with both hands clear. The numerical simulation checks and physical trial procedure are in the README.
reset_notes: From the center of the tabletop use (x, y) in mm, with +x away from the arms and +y toward the left arm. Lamp (−58, 0), harp rest (−203, 0), shade (+5, +183), loose finial (−45, −159). The rest length and saddle channel spacing are along y. The lamp sits with an empty saddle, the harp stands in both rest channels with sleeves down, and the shade stands on its large rim with a spider spoke toward +x.
fidelity: The README specifies a mechanical fixture using named commercial parts and a dimensioned shade. Simulation dimensions approximate the Paxton harp and hardware. Wire flex uses passive springs. The independent sleeves slide by physical contact, and the harp supports the washer by contact. A physical specimen has not been tested. The task ends before finial attachment.
